notes: Total 18 -> hard bucket. The pipeline is genuinely multi-stage (dependent_stages=2): detect the single-byte XOR transform from the journal header and reverse it, merge surviving DB rows (checkpointed) with un-checkpointed journal rows, then run a four-step SQL cleaning pipeline (lowercase name, digits-only CAST into a new column, delete rows missing both contact fields, ROW_NUMBER de-dup by id keeping first), then sort + de-dup for JSON/CSV export. reasoning_depth=3 comes from inferring the transform from header bytes, choosing the merge order so de-duplication is deterministic, and keeping the whole codec robust when malformed journal lines, empty journals, no-digit msisdn, and duplicate ids all occur at once. hidden_case_generalization=3: the verifier re-runs /app/recover.py on five freshly generated hidden scenarios (varied n, journal_share, dup_share, malformed-line counts), the open-fd and perf subcommands, and reqires exact JSON/CSV equality. quantitative_correctness=3 enforces exact equality, id-uniqueness and ordering. resource_pressure=2 reflects an indexed-query perf gate on a bare >=1M-row scaled DB after warm-up plus a 1.2M-row hidden perf DB. /app/merged.json, /app/trial_*.csv and /app/fd.txt are produced by running recover.py, never hand-written. The task floor is the max competency floor (medium); difficulty (hard) is >= that floor, documented_probe is null.
